title: From Connectivity to Rewards: Dense Reward Learning with Directed State Graphs
abstract: arXiv:2609.10781v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The integration of graphs with Goal-Conditioned Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (GCHRL) has received increasing attention, as graphs naturally encode task hierarchies for effective subgoal sampling. However, existing methods often overlook intrinsic connectivity information, failing to fully leverage the underlying topology for efficient learning. Most graph-based GCHRL methods use the graph as a stochastic sampling tool rather than as an environmental model that encodes connectivity and state-accessibility information. This limitation is particularly acute in quasimetric environments, where the inherent asymmetry of state transitions poses a fundamental challenge to stable policy learning and robust path planning. In this paper, we address these problems by introducing a state connectivity model designed to predict pairwise state connectivity strength in asymmetric environments. translated_title: 从连通性到奖励：基于有向状态图的密集奖励学习
translated_abstract: 图与目标条件分层强化学习的结合受到了越来越多的关注，因为图能够自然地编码任务层次结构，从而实现有效的子目标采样。然而，现有方法往往忽视了内在的连通性信息，未能充分利用底层拓扑结构来实现高效学习。大多数基于图的GCHRL方法仅将图用作随机采样工具，而非将其作为编码连通性和状态可达性信息的环境模型。这一局限性在拟度量（quasimetric）环境中尤为突出，因为状态转移固有的不对称性对稳定的策略学习和鲁棒的路径规划构成了根本性挑战。在本文中，我们通过引入一个状态连通性模型来解决这些问题，该模型旨在预测非对称环境中成对状态之间的连通强度。我们将这些连通强度转换为标量（奖励），从而……
tldr: 该论文提出一种状态连通性模型，利用有向状态图预测非对称环境中的成对状态连通强度，并将其转化为密集奖励信号，从而提升目标条件分层强化学习中策略学习与路径规划的稳定性与鲁棒性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a state connectivity model that predicts pairwise state connectivity strength in asymmetric environments using directed state graphs, transforming connectivity into dense reward signals to improve stable policy learning and robust path planning in goal-conditioned hierarchical reinforcement learning.
